questions.q: Where does the actual AWS bill and invoices live?
options: The Billing and Cost Management console
AWS CloudTrail
The IAM console
CloudWatch Logs
questions.explain: Billing and Cost Management is the source of truth for the bill itself, invoices, payment methods, and the running total for the current period.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a dimension Cost Explorer lets you group or filter spend by?
options: IAM password policy
Service
Linked account
Tag
questions.explain: Cost Explorer groups and filters by service, linked account, Region, and tag — not by an IAM password policy, which has nothing to do with spend.

questions.q: What does Cost Explorer's forecast actually do?
options: Projects future spend by extrapolating from historical usage patterns
Automatically cancels resources before they get too expensive
Predicts upcoming projects that haven't started yet
Only shows spend from the previous calendar year
questions.explain: The forecast extrapolates from past usage — it has no awareness of a new project or migration nobody has told it about yet.

questions.q: A bill spikes unexpectedly. What's an effective first step in Cost Explorer to find the cause?
options: Group the current period's spend by service to see which service is driving the increase
Delete the account and create a new one
Disable Cost Explorer so the spike stops showing
Change the AWS Region
questions.explain: Grouping by service narrows the spike to a specific service, which can then be filtered further and grouped by tag to find the responsible project.

questions.q: Why does grouping spend by tag answer a different question than grouping by service?
options: Tag grouping shows which project or team is driving cost, even when that project spans multiple services
Tags and services always show identical results
Tag grouping only works for S3 buckets
Tags cannot be used in Cost Explorer at all
questions.explain: A service-only view can't attribute cost to a specific project once that project touches several services; tags (from Chapter 5) solve exactly that.
